slot.brief: Find the locus of z satisfying arg((z − α)/(z − β)) = π/2; derive the circle with α, β as endpoints of a diameter.

verdicts.working: arg((z-A)/(z-B)) = π/2 with A = 4+3i, B = -2-5i means z lies on the circle with AB as diameter (the arc giving +π/2). Center = midpoint (A+B)/2 = 1 - i; radius = |A-B|/2 = |6+8i|/2 = 5. So |z - (1 - i)| = |z - 1 + i| = 5, verified numerically (phase = +π/2 on the appropriate arc). Option A.

working:
The given equation is $\arg\left(\dfrac{z - \alpha}{z - \beta}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, where $\alpha = 4 + 3i$ and $\beta = -2 - 5i$.

Geometrically, this represents a semicircle having the line segment joining $\alpha$ and $\beta$ as its diameter.

The center $z_0$ of the circle is the midpoint of $\alpha$ and $\beta$:
$$z_0 = \dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2} = \dfrac{(4 + 3i) + (-2 - 5i)}{2} = \dfrac{2 - 2i}{2} = 1 - i$$

The radius $R$ of the circle is half the distance between $\alpha$ and $\beta$:
$$R = \dfrac{|\alpha - \beta|}{2} = \dfrac{|(4 + 3i) - (-2 - 5i)|}{2} = \dfrac{|6 + 8i|}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2}}{2} = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5$$

Thus, any point $z$ on this locus lies on the circle:
$$|z - z_0| = R \implies |z - (1 - i)| = 5 \implies |z - 1 + i| = 5$$
